measures.title: Referred measure to dedicate sales tax for community facilities, including libraries and recreation and community centers
measures.summary: Creates a new 0.129% City of Aurora sales and use tax (12.9 cents on every $100 purchase) from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2057, raising up to $12,640,000 in the first year, for community facilities, including libraries and recreation and community centers. It also allows the city to issue up to $105,000,000 in revenue bonds, with a maximum repayment cost of $204,870,000, repaid from the new tax, for projects such as park renovations and new parks, recreation center improvements and new recreation centers, and library improvements and new libraries. The city could keep and spend all revenue from the tax as a voter-approved revenue change.
measures.yesMeans: Aurora adds the 0.129% sales and use tax through 2057 and may issue the stated bonds for community facilities, including libraries and recreation and community centers.
measures.noMeans: The new sales and use tax and bonds are not approved.

measures.title: Referred measure to dedicate sales tax for public safety infrastructure and facilities
measures.summary: Creates a new 0.064% City of Aurora sales and use tax (6.4 cents on every $100 purchase) from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2057, raising up to $6,270,000 in the first year, for public safety infrastructure and facilities. It also allows the city to issue up to $53,000,000 in revenue bonds, with a maximum repayment cost of $101,600,000, repaid from the new tax, for projects such as fire station renovations and remodels and Aurora 911 and police facility improvements. The city could keep and spend all revenue from the tax as a voter-approved revenue change.
measures.yesMeans: Aurora adds the 0.064% sales and use tax through 2057 and may issue the stated bonds for public safety infrastructure and facilities.
measures.noMeans: The new sales and use tax and bonds are not approved.

measures.title: Referred measure to dedicate sales tax for transportation infrastructure and facilities
measures.summary: Creates a new 0.132% City of Aurora sales and use tax (13.2 cents on every $100 purchase) from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2057, raising up to $12,940,000 in the first year, for transportation infrastructure and facilities. It also allows the city to issue up to $108,000,000 in revenue bonds, with a maximum repayment cost of $209,733,000, repaid from the new tax, for projects such as traffic, intersection and pedestrian safety improvements, major bridge replacements, and roadway improvements and expansion. The city could keep and spend all revenue from the tax as a voter-approved revenue change.
measures.yesMeans: Aurora adds the 0.132% sales and use tax through 2057 and may issue the stated bonds for transportation infrastructure and facilities.
measures.noMeans: The new sales and use tax and bonds are not approved.

measures.title: Referred measure to move the City of Aurora's regular municipal elections to even-numbered years
measures.summary: Amends the Aurora City Charter to move regular municipal elections from odd-numbered years to even-numbered years. It also amends the Charter to allow one-time shortened terms of office needed to make the transition.
measures.yesMeans: Aurora's regular city elections move to even-numbered years, with some terms shortened once to make the change.
measures.noMeans: Aurora's regular city elections stay in odd-numbered years.
